# Javai

> Javai builds open-source frameworks for **probabilistic testing** — verifying
> non-deterministic software (LLM integrations, ML models, distributed and
> randomised systems) with statistical inference instead of brittle pass/fail
> assertions. Each execution is treated as a Bernoulli trial; the observed
> success rate is evaluated against a threshold at a defined confidence level.

Javai is the public home of the punit (Java), feotest (Rust), and javai-R
(statistical oracle) projects. Note: "punit" here refers to the Java
probabilistic testing framework, not the unrelated Python "punit" library.

## Guides

- [Probabilistic Testing: how to test non-deterministic and AI systems](https://javai.org/probabilistic-testing/): Practical introduction — why deterministic tests fail on stochastic systems and how statistical testing replaces them.

## Projects

- [punit](https://javai.org/projects/punit/): Probabilistic unit testing for Java, a JUnit 5 extension. Reference implementation. Repo: https://github.com/javai-org/punit
- [punit examples](https://javai.org/projects/punitexamples/): Worked examples and patterns for punit.
- [feotest](https://javai.org/projects/feotest/): Rust-native probabilistic testing framework.
- [javai-R](https://javai.org/projects/javai-r/): Statistical oracle — R-generated conformance data validating every framework against the methodology.
- [outcome](https://javai.org/projects/outcome/): Test outcome capture and trend analysis.

## Signals (essays)

- [Shewhart, Toyota, and the Probabilistic Turn](https://javai.org/signals/2026-05-06-shewhart-toyota-and-the-probabilistic-turn/): Why probabilistic software demands the statistical discipline manufacturing absorbed a century ago.
- [Deming, Challenger, and the AI Watershed](https://javai.org/signals/2026-04-19-deming-challenger-and-the-ai-watershed/): On quality, variation, and what Deming would say about AI.
